cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took away a chair like the caterer did. The cake can sit on the piano stool, and your uncle can have the window seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She took away a broken chair. You've removed the only spare seat for the pianist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, making a little room. The pianist can sit at the window until we're ready for music.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Uncle's there, leaning against the window. He has to move so I can open it; the cake's icing is melting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring my chair back for Uncle. Then open his window for the cake, and I'll hold the cake while the pianist takes the stool.

reason: Specify that Uncle blocks the window, not an unexplained movable seat, and make each final move physically possible: chair for Uncle, open window, A holds cake to free pianist stool. Remove mechanism-summary sentence.
